destinations.name: At-Bashy
destinations.short: Our home valley: gorges, pastures and the road to Tash-Rabat
destinations.about: At-Bashy is our home: a valley in the Naryn region between the At-Bashy and Jaman-Too ranges, with gorges, summer pastures and the road south to Tash-Rabat and Chatyr-Kol. It is also the gateway to Kel-Suu Lake in the Kok-Kiya valley near the Chinese border.

highlights.d: Stone caravanserai in a quiet side valley, once a stop on the Silk Road.
High plateau lake near the Torugart road, with wide views of the ranges.
The valley where our horse routes begin, with dramatic rock walls.

destinations.gettingThere: We pick you up in Bishkek and drive via Kochkor and Naryn to At-Bashy. The drive takes most of a day with stops on the way.
gettingThereBullets: Private car transfer from Bishkek (included in tours)
Shared taxi to Naryn from Bishkek's western bus station

destinations.name: Naryn
destinations.short: The high inner Tien Shan — gateway to Kel-Suu and Song-Kul
destinations.about: Naryn region covers the high inner Tien Shan: wide river valleys, summer pastures above 3,000 m and the roads that lead to Song-Kul, Kel-Suu and the old Silk Road post of Tash-Rabat. It is the least visited and most scenic part of Kyrgyzstan.

highlights.d: The regional hub and starting point for most high-mountain routes.
Where the two Naryn rivers meet, surrounded by steep canyon walls.
Jailoos where shepherd families move with their herds every summer.

destinations.gettingThere: Naryn town is reached via the Bishkek–Torugart highway, a scenic drive over the Dolon pass. From there, smaller roads and 4x4 tracks lead into the mountains.
gettingThereBullets: Private car transfer from Bishkek (included in tours)
Shared taxi from Bishkek's western bus station
4x4 required beyond Naryn town for most routes

destinations.name: Kel-Suu
destinations.short: A turquoise lake at 3,500 m between granite walls
destinations.about: Kel-Suu is a turquoise alpine lake sitting at about 3,500 m in the Kok-Kiya valley, close to the Chinese border. It is reached on horseback over the Bogoshtu Pass or by 4x4 via Tash-Rabat and Aksay — one of the most remote and dramatic places in Kyrgyzstan.

info.v: ≈ 8–9 hours by car, plus a ride or drive in

highlights.d: The high pass crossed on the direct horse trek from At-Bashy.
Turquoise water between granite walls, with almost no other visitors.
Kel-Suu sits in a restricted border area; we arrange the permit for you.

destinations.gettingThere: Kel-Suu is reached either by a multi-day horse trek over the Bogoshtu Pass, or by 4x4 via Tash-Rabat, Arpa and Aksay, arriving at the shore directly.
gettingThereBullets: Horse trek via Bogoshtu Pass (3–4 days from At-Bashy)
4x4 route via Tash-Rabat and Aksay (1–2 days from Bishkek)
Border permit arranged by us — passport details needed in advance

destinations.name: Song-Kul
destinations.short: Alpine lake and summer yurt camps of shepherd families
destinations.about: Song-Kul is a high alpine lake at about 3,000 m surrounded by open pastures. Every summer, shepherd families move up with their herds and set up yurt camps along the shore — it is one of the best places in Kyrgyzstan to experience nomadic life firsthand.

highlights.d: Stay with shepherd families in traditional yurts by the lake.
Easy rides around the shore and up into the surrounding pastures.
The light over the lake at dawn and dusk is a highlight for photographers.

destinations.gettingThere: Song-Kul is reached via Kochkor by 4x4 or on horseback, climbing over the Kalmak-Ashuu or Moldo-Ashuu passes onto the plateau.
gettingThereBullets: Private car/4x4 transfer from Bishkek (included in tours)
Shared taxi to Kochkor from Bishkek, then 4x4 onward
Horseback approach available from several trailheads

destinations.name: Issyk-Kul
destinations.short: The great lake, canyons and gorges of the Tien Shan
destinations.about: Issyk-Kul is one of the largest alpine lakes in the world, ringed by the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges. Around it are red-rock canyons, gorges, hot springs and the town of Karakol — a good add-on to a mountain trip or a relaxed stop on the way east.

highlights.d: Red sandstone formations on the lake's southern shore.
The 'Seven Bulls' red rock ridge near Karakol.
The regional town, gateway to the Terskey Ala-Too for onward trekking.

destinations.gettingThere: Issyk-Kul is reached via the Bishkek–Balykchy road along either the northern or southern shore, both scenic drives of half a day.
gettingThereBullets: Private car transfer from Bishkek (included in tours)
Shared taxi or marshrutka from Bishkek's Vostok-5 station
Northern shore (Cholpon-Ata) or southern shore (Bokonbaevo) routes

destinations.name: Sary-Chelek, Arslanbob & Osh
destinations.short: Forests, walnut groves and the ancient south
destinations.about: The south of Kyrgyzstan is a different country again: the Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve's mountain lakes, the world's largest walnut forest at Arslanbob, and the ancient city of Osh with its bazaar and Sulaiman-Too. A green, forested contrast to the high Naryn plateau.

info.v: ≈ 10–12 hours by car, or a short flight to Osh

highlights.d: A chain of mountain lakes inside a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
The largest natural walnut forest in the world, with waterfalls and viewpoints.
Central Asia's oldest city, its bazaar and the sacred Sulaiman-Too mountain.

destinations.gettingThere: Most travelers fly from Bishkek to Osh (about 1 hour), then continue by car to Arslanbob and Sary-Chelek. Overland travel from Bishkek is also possible via the Osh highway.
gettingThereBullets: Private car transfer from Osh (included in tours)
Overland via the Bishkek–Osh highway (10–12 hours)
